title: Sunny and the Bush Mouse | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka watches a tiny native bush mouse carry a seed across a moonlit clearing, holding it carefully with both tiny paws — the most determined little traveller in the whole bush. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny was standing very quietly at the edge of the clearing when she saw the bush mouse.

It was tiny. So tiny that at first she thought it was a large spider — until it moved, and she could see the small round ears and the long thin tail and the quick bright eyes.

The mouse was carrying something. A seed — large and round, nearly as big as its head — held in both front paws as it scurried across the moonlit clearing.

Sunny watched.

The mouse moved in quick little bursts — three steps, pause, look around, three more steps, pause — navigating the clearing with great focus and determination.

It reached a tuft of grass and disappeared inside for a moment. Then it came back out, without the seed, and scurried off in another direction.

Gone.

Sunny stood at the edge of the clearing, smiling.

The mouse had been so intent on its small task. So thoroughly absorbed. It had not seen Sunny at all — or if it had, it had decided Sunny didn't matter right now, because there was a seed to be carried, and that was the most important thing.

Sunny thought: everyone has their own important things to do, even at night.

She sat down in the soft grass at the edge of the clearing and looked out at the quiet, now-empty patch where the mouse had been.

The moonlight lay still on the grass.

And she fell asleep to the thought of a very small mouse in a very cosy nest with its seed.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, bush mouse. Goodnight, little one.
